## 1.6.0 (2026-11-15)

- Persist immutable ticket due times and backfill existing tickets before serving requests.

Due times are calculated and saved even with the feature off. Response hours must be whole numbers from 0 to 876000.

p=Path('docs/api.md');s=p.read_text();s+='
## Due times (optional)

With `DUE_TIMES=on`, every ticket response includes `due`, an ISO UTC timestamp fixed at creation.
`GET /tickets?overdue=true` returns only open or in-progress tickets with `due` strictly before the current time.
It combines with status, priority, assignee and cursor pagination. `overdue=false` applies no overdue filter;
other values return 400. While the feature is off, `due` is omitted and the overdue parameter is ignored.
';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/operations.md');s=p.read_text();s+='
## Rolling out due times

1. Back up `DATA_FILE`, stop the old service and deploy 1.6.0 with `DUE_TIMES` unset. Configure
   `RESPONSE_HOURS_URGENT`, `RESPONSE_HOURS_HIGH`, `RESPONSE_HOURS_NORMAL` and `RESPONSE_HOURS_LOW` if needed.
2. Start the service. Before accepting requests it atomically saves missing due times for every existing ticket,
   using each ticket's own creation timestamp and priority. A failed save prevents startup. Check the data file
   contains `due` on every ticket. API responses remain unchanged while the switch is off.
3. Restart with `DUE_TIMES=on` to expose the persisted values and enable overdue filtering.

Due times are saved once and retained across priority edits, hours changes and restarts. They are also saved
for new tickets and imports while the switch is off. Backfill changes no audit history or notifications.

To roll back, stop this service and start 1.4.0 against the same data file: its version remains 1, and optional
fields are ignored, so all tickets remain visible. The old release drops unknown fields when it saves; preserve
a backup if the original due times must be recovered on a later upgrade. Only one process may own the file.
';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/decisions/0010-due-times.md');p.write_text('''# 10. Persisted due times with staged activation

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Response promises must survive changes to priority and policy. Operators need an off-by-default rollout and rollback to 1.4.0.

## Decision

Store an optional ISO `due` on each ticket in version-1 data. At startup, derive missing values from creation and
priority, and atomically save the backfill before exposing the store. This runs even with the feature off. New tickets
and imports always save a due time. Policy hours come from `RESPONSE_HOURS_*` environment settings; saved values never
change. Backfill is derived metadata and does not change audit history, updated timestamps, or notifications.

`DUE_TIMES=on` exposes due times and enables overdue filtering, using the injected clock, strictly past due and active
status. Otherwise the response representation and query behavior remain as before. All listing filters intersect before pagination.

## Consequences

Version 1.4.0 accepts the same file and ignores optional fields, retaining all tickets. Its writes discard unknown
fields, so retaining due promises across an extended rollback requires preserving a backup. No incompatible format
version or extra required records are introduced. Command-line raw columns retain their positions.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');s=p.read_text();s+='| 10 | [Persisted due times](0010-due-times.md) | Accepted |
';p.write_text(s)
